response.final_text:
**Proposed disposition:** CLOSE_FP, confidence 0.78. It is recorded as a proposal, awaiting a human decision (case C-A-261005-0009).

**Three facts that drove it:**
1. The 21,768 BUY ICEBERG was trading before any opposite-side trade. 5,835 were filled (27% of the order, against an opposite trade of only 544), so the resting order was working.
2. The 544 SELL was under a different parent order (C-T-X1005-05-B). The BUY iceberg sits under C-T-X1005-05-A, and this is an agency desk. That makes them different clients' orders, not one round trip. The iceberg's size was hidden, so it could not signal to the market. There was also no reversion after the cancel, no repetition in the session, and no prior alerts.
3. The iceberg was 8.97 times the average depth, but size alone is not a spoofing feature under the closure standard.

**What would change my mind:** evidence that the BUY and SELL parents are the same client or the same decision, or a repeat of the one-sided cycle on other sessions.

I did note the +3 tick favourable move before the sell. I did not treat it as a benefit, for the reasons in fact 2.
